question: When price first reaches a 09:30 GEX PRO level during the cash session, is it rejected more often than at a random level the same distance from the open?

inputs.sessions: every graded session on the track-record branch (sessions/<date>_<market>.json) that has its 1-minute record, NQ and ES (every archive day so far is also there; archive-only days need their own loader and a new version)

levels.C1-C3: the 09:30 paste's R token: the first three C entries in the order written (the paste ranks them)
levels.P1-P3: the 09:30 paste's R token: the first three P entries in the order written

inputs.levels_unit: index points, as computed and frozen before 09:30 (plan.asof < 09:30 ET: lookahead_audit L1; paste ts < 09:30: L5)
inputs.bars: the session's 1-minute futures record (minutes/<date>_<market>.json): [minute after 09:30, high, low, close], 09:30 to the close (13:00 on early closes, from marketcal)
inputs.mapping: level_fut = level_index x ratio, ratio = futures 09:30 open / index 09:30 open, as stored in the minutes record (known at 09:30; the indicator maps the same way). One factor per session, never a later one.
inputs.open: index_open x ratio (the futures price at 09:30)
inputs.previous_close: the previous trading day's graded index close x today's ratio (marketcal.previous_trading_day); none on the first recorded day

rules.side: above if level_fut > open + tol, below if level_fut < open - tol; within tol of the open = 'at_open' (no side: own category, never a touch)
rules.gap_through: level_fut strictly between previous_close and open (price passed it overnight): own category, never a touch; unknown on the first recorded day (category 'no_prior_close')
rules.touch: the first bar whose high >= level_fut - tol (level above) or low <= level_fut + tol (level below)
rules.reject: after the touch bar, price trades k x tol back from the level (low <= level_fut - k x tol above; high >= level_fut + k x tol below) before any bar closes beyond the level by tol
rules.break: a bar from the touch bar on closes beyond the level by tol (close > level_fut + tol above; close < level_fut - tol below) before a reject
rules.same_bar: a bar that both closes beyond (break) and trades k x tol back (reject) counts as a break
rules.stall: neither within 60 minutes after the touch bar, or by the close if sooner
rules.resolution_minutes: minutes from the touch bar to the deciding bar (stall: none)
rules.excursions: from the touch bar's minute, for h = 15, 30, 60: max move away = max distance traded back from the level in the reject direction; max move through = max distance traded beyond the level; points and em_fut units; a horizon past the close is not reported for that touch
rules.cluster: levels of one session and market within tol of each other form a cluster; its first member in the order ZG, CW, PW, Ab1, C1, C2, C3, P1, P2, P3 is counted, the others are reported only as 'dependent' and excluded from the headline rates

baseline.draws: for each market and level type: 1000 random levels (at least 200 required), seed 20261118
baseline.how: pick a session uniformly from the sessions where that level type exists; pick a signed distance (in em_fut, side included) uniformly from that market's real distances of that type; random level = open + distance x em_fut, in that session
baseline.rules: the same tol, side, gap_through, touch, outcome and cluster rules (a random level within tol of a real level of that session is dropped and redrawn)

statistics.reject_rate: rejects / touches (touches exclude at_open, gap_through, untouched, dependent)
statistics.difference: real reject rate - baseline reject rate, per level type x market
statistics.unit: the session: per session (real rejects, real touches, baseline rejects, baseline touches); resampling sessions, never touches
statistics.interval: 95%: 10,000 session resamples, seed 20261118; expanded percentile interval (Hesterberg: tails at z = sqrt(S/(S-1)) x t_0.975(S-1) for S sessions), or BCa (jackknife over sessions, same z) when |z0| > 0.25; the method is named (gexpro/uncertainty.py)
statistics.p_value: two-sided against no difference, from the same resamples: 2 x the smaller share at or beyond 0, +1 smoothing; labelled a p-value
statistics.power: sessions needed for 80% power at alpha 0.05: S x (z_0.975 + z_0.8)^2 x bootstrap variance / difference^2; labelled optimistic
statistics.headline: an interval that includes 0 reads: no proven edge yet (n sessions)
statistics.method_check: tools/stress/uncertainty_coverage.py: 1,000 synthetic datasets with a known effect and day-level clustering; coverage must be 93-97%
statistics.small_cells: fewer than 20 touches: shown as n<20, greyed, never ranked, no interval

robustness: levels shifted +5 / -5 NQ points and +1 / -1 ES point (the measured overnight basis miss): the table is rerun and shown beside
roll weeks (marketcal.roll_date to the quarterly expiry) flagged; results with and without them
reporting: every table shows n (sessions and touches), the data-through date and this file's SHA-256
verification: the verifier re-derives every touch and outcome of 3 sessions (one quiet, one trend, one with a gap-through) from the raw bars; 100% agreement required
verdict_rule: an edge is claimed only for a level type x market with n >= 20 touches whose interval excludes 0; otherwise 'no proven edge yet (n sessions)' or 'not enough data'
changes: v2 (Phase 4): the statistics only; inputs, rules and baseline are v1's, so v1 and v2 classify every level identically
